name: MPD Default
description: Auto-routed by the complexity gate (sessionTeamPolicy.autoRoute; staged — the captain designs the roster/DAG, then the user reviews and approves the plan in the Web panel).

profile.name: mpd
profile.description: The specialist roster surfaced as normal-named teammate templates — captain-planned (roster only; the captain designs the DAG during the staged plan).
profile.protocol: Read-only members (Architect, Researcher, Planner, Explorer, Plan Reviewer, Vision Analyst) take requirements/review/analysis tasks only and never edit files. Workers (Senior Engineer, Junior Engineer, Deep Worker, Lead, Reviewer) take implementation/verification/integration. The captain leads, designs the DAG, and integrates results. Workmate reuse: before delegating a role task, consult mpd_workmate_list / mpd_workmate_match(task); if a workmate note matches well, delegate to that workmate (member name = workmate name, so its persona/memory are injected), otherwise initialize a fresh workmate with mpd_workmate_init — never force a weak note match.

members.name: Architect
members.executionPrompt: Read-only architecture advisor. You advise, others execute — never edit files. Favor simplicity and existing patterns; give one clear recommendation with concise rationale and evidence.

members.name: Researcher
members.executionPrompt: Read-only researcher. Gather evidence from the codebase, AST/LSP and web sources; cite file:line and URLs; never edit files or invent findings.

members.name: Reviewer
members.executionPrompt: Deep reviewer. Produce correctness/risk findings with evidence; recommend fixes but do not apply them.

members.name: Senior Engineer
members.executionPrompt: Primary engineer. Plan small, execute with tools, keep diffs minimal, verify every change, report honestly.

tasks.subject: Gate audit: classify every legacy plugin-spec reference, and test the patch's completeness
tasks.description:
Read-only analysis seat. If bash is denied to you, satisfy the verify commands through the grep/glob/read tools and report them with status "reported", quoting the equivalent evidence. Your deliverable is a long text: attach it with the task-artifact channel at evidence/audit/gate-audit.md (read-only seats may write under evidence/** only). Reference paths are read-only: /root/dshProj/tui/dsh-TUI (host) and /root/dshProj/tui/dsh-TUI/dsh-ecosystem-spec (pristine submodule). The working copy you audit against is dsh-ecosystem-spec/ in the workspace. The trap to test explicitly: the string appears 4 times but only 2 are stale.

VERDICT SEMANTICS (kind=requirements): verdict=pass means THIS AUDIT is complete and evidence-backed — it does NOT mean the tree is perfect. If you discover a stale reference the patch misses, report it as a finding (acceptance item 6) and still submit verdict=pass. Only submit needs_revision if the audit itself could not be completed, and then you must include structured findings (id, severity, problem, requiredFix) and the task will fail.
tasks.objective: Produce an evidence-backed gate audit, attached as evidence/audit/gate-audit.md, answering from the bytes on disk: (1) every place the legacy token `plugin-spec` appears in the target repo dsh-ecosystem-spec (excluding vendor/ and .git/) and in the host repo dsh-TUI's scripts/ and package.json, each classified as load-bearing (a gate that must keep naming the legacy path) or stale documentation (a doc that must be corrected); (2) whether the rename src/plugin-spec -> src/adapter/standard is real and complete, juxtaposing the canonical module list against the legacy-shim list the gates themselves assert absent; (3) whether upstream/adapter-cross-repo-sync.patch is a COMPLETE sweep of the stale references in dsh-ecosystem-spec, or whether it misses any, naming file:line for anything missed; (4) whether either patched doc is reachable from any boot-visible artifact. READ FIRST: /tmp/mpd-sst-rzQJpS/side/complex/2/ws/evidence/ENVIRONMENT.md — it pins the read-only reference paths, the measured baseline facts, and the gate/boot commands. This task is analysis only: report findings, never fix them.
acceptance: Every occurrence of the token `plugin-spec` in dsh-ecosystem-spec (excluding vendor/ and .git/) is listed with file:line, the exact line, and a classification (load-bearing gate name vs stale path) each with a one-line reason.

The patch's claims are checked line by line against that list: exactly which occurrences it changes, which it leaves, and why leaving them is correct — the npm script name `verify:plugin-spec` must be shown to still exist in the host package.json so that leaving it is justified.

The canonical-path claim is verified against disk (src/plugin-spec absent, src/adapter/standard present in the host repo), with the canonical module list set beside the legacy-shim list that scripts/verify-adapter-skeleton.ts and scripts/verify-compat-removal.ts assert absent.
Every host gate that names the legacy path is classified with file:line and the direction of its assertion (asserts-absent vs asserts-present), so nobody 'fixes' a load-bearing gate.

A boot-impact section states, with the read or command that produced it, whether either patched doc is present in the installed payload under /root/.nvm/versions/node/v24.16.0/lib/node_modules/@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui/.

Any stale reference the patch does NOT cover is reported as an explicit finding with file:line and severity — reported, never silently fixed (the implementation task's inScope is the two doc files only).
The audit is attached as evidence/audit/gate-audit.md; every claim carries the file:line or command that produced it, and anything not measured is labelled INFERRED.

tasks.subject: Apply the cross-repo sync patch to the spec working copy
tasks.description: The patch is the artifact: apply it with git apply, do not hand-edit around it and do not edit the patch itself. Read evidence/ENVIRONMENT.md first — it pins the exact gate and boot commands, the baseline digests, and the vendor/dsh-std offline stand-in. Chain the three gates with && or capture each exit code separately so a failure is never masked. If the audit (t1) reports a stale reference the patch misses, do NOT widen scope: report it in your completion output and leave it to the captain.
tasks.objective: Apply upstream/adapter-cross-repo-sync.patch to the workspace working copy dsh-ecosystem-spec/ so the two stale documentation references name the canonical `src/adapter/standard/` path, and nothing else in the tree changes. Inputs: upstream/adapter-cross-repo-sync.patch (the patch), evidence/audit/gate-audit.md (the classification of what must and must not change), and evidence/ENVIRONMENT.md (the pinned commands and baseline digests).
acceptance: `git -C dsh-ecosystem-spec apply` succeeds on the pristine baseline (commit 147fc3f); if it does not, stop and report the conflict verbatim instead of adapting or rewriting the patch.
`git -C dsh-ecosystem-spec diff --stat` reports exactly 2 files changed, 1 insertion and 1 deletion each, and `git status --porcelain` shows no other path in the working copy modified.

The final bytes of dsh-ecosystem-spec/adapters/dsh-tui-v0.15.md:6 and dsh-ecosystem-spec/docs/plugin-admission-and-development.md:132 name `src/adapter/standard/`, read back from the working tree (never from the patch text).
The two `verify:plugin-spec` npm-script occurrences (adapters/dsh-tui-v0.15.md:120 and docs/plugin-admission-and-development.md:130) are byte-unchanged; state the check that proves it.

`node scripts/conformance.mjs --standalone --no-build` exits 0 and `node conformance/tests/validate-manifest.cli.test.js` exits 0 on the patched tree, with raw output saved under evidence/implementation/.

The host composition control (env HOME=$PWD/.sandbox/home DSH_HOME=$PWD/.sandbox/dshhome dsh --profile dsh-tui --dump-config, run from the workspace root) exits 0 and its dump is byte-identical to evidence/baseline-composition.log (sha256 26892a0fe8f4e527e0cbcb611ad038623ecb83c7ff83b44e26054801a6bc4016).

evidence/implementation/ holds the command log with exit codes, the diff, and the before/after digests; the completion payload reports commandsRun for every verify command and changedPaths for exactly the two doc files.
verify: git -C dsh-ecosystem-spec diff --stat && git -C dsh-ecosystem-spec status --porcelain

tasks.subject: Independently verify the applied change and the boot plane
tasks.description: Reproduce, do not trust: run every command yourself from your own invocation, including the two spec gates and the composition control. Read evidence/ENVIRONMENT.md for the pinned commands and the baseline digests, and evidence/audit/gate-audit.md for the classification you are testing. Do NOT edit the two docs or anything else the change owns — if you find a defect, report it as a finding and let the repair route own the fix. A confirmation-only pass is a failed verification: the falsification attempts are the point.
tasks.objective: Independently verify, on the current bytes, the two claims the change rests on: (a) that the applied edit is exactly the intended rename and touches nothing a gate or a boot path reads; (b) that the host boot plane is unaffected. Re-run both spec gates and the composition control yourself, and actively try to falsify the 'docs-only / off the boot path' claim rather than confirming it.
acceptance: Both spec gates are re-run by you on the patched tree and their exit codes are reported verbatim; if you cite the JSON report, state the assertion semantics from conformance/tests/run.js (expected-pass vs expected-fail fixtures) instead of the raw pass field.

The docs-only claim is upheld or falsified with evidence: `git -C dsh-ecosystem-spec diff --stat` and `git status --porcelain` are quoted, and it is shown that no file under conformance/, registry/, protocols/, schemas/, scripts/ or vendor/ changed.

The off-the-boot-path claim is TESTED, not assumed: a command shows neither patched doc exists anywhere in the installed payload under /root/.nvm/versions/node/v24.16.0/lib/node_modules/@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui/, and the post-change composition dump is compared by sha256 against the baseline digest 26892a0fe8f4e527e0cbcb611ad038623ecb83c7ff83b44e26054801a6bc4016.
The rename's correctness is independently re-derived from disk (src/plugin-spec absent, src/adapter/standard present) rather than taken from the audit or from the patch's own text.

At least one genuine falsification attempt is recorded with its result, including a negative result — for example grepping the installed payload and the host source for readers of the two patched doc filenames, or checking whether any gate/script/config in either repo references adapters/dsh-tui-v0.15.md.

The honest limit is stated explicitly: `dsh --profile dsh-tui --dump-config` composes rows and never executes plugin code, and no live session boot is reachable here (no credentials/model route), so the boot claim is scoped to the composition plane plus payload absence.
Evidence lands under evidence/verification/, and the completion payload carries commandsRun with real exit codes plus an acceptanceResults entry per criterion.
verify: git -C dsh-ecosystem-spec diff --stat && git -C dsh-ecosystem-spec status --porcelain

tasks.subject: Review the cross-repo sync implementation against its contract
tasks.description: Read-only quality gate. Judge the implementation on its latest bytes: evidence/audit/gate-audit.md (the classification), the working-tree diff, and evidence/verification/ (the independent re-run). Do not edit anything — read-only seats attach under evidence/** only. If the implementation is honest and complete, verdict=pass completes this task; if a criterion is unmet or a claim is unsupported, you must return needs_revision or reject WITH structured findings and fail the task.
tasks.objective: Judge whether applying upstream/adapter-cross-repo-sync.patch satisfied the user's step 3 and its contract: the two stale references now name the canonical path, the two npm-script-name occurrences are untouched, the change is confined to the two declared files, and the audit plus verification evidence actually supports those claims. Do not accept a claim you cannot trace to a file:line, a command, or a digest.
acceptance: The two changed lines are quoted from the working tree (not from the patch text) and shown to name `src/adapter/standard/`.
The two `verify:plugin-spec` npm-script occurrences are quoted and shown unchanged, and the review states why renaming them would be wrong (that script name still exists in the host package.json).
Scope discipline is checked on the working tree: no file outside the two declared docs was modified, and dsh-ecosystem-spec/vendor/ (the offline std stand-in) is untracked and absent from the diff.

The review states explicitly whether the change can reach the boot plane, on the strength of the payload check, and flags any over-claiming it finds in the other members' evidence (for example a boot claim that outruns what --dump-config can prove).
The review records what it inspected (file:line, commands, digests) so the verdict is falsifiable, and lands it under evidence/review/.
